messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Polish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Polish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table (Italian → Polish)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | mosse | “initial moment / first hour” (noun, plural) | **chwila** | “moment / hour” | OK | | di (line 40) | genitive marker “of” linking *mosse* and *prima* | — (case ending on *pierwsza*) | — | UNNECESSARY | | prima | “first” (adjective) | **pierwsza** | “first” | OK | | quelle | demonstrative “those” (plural) | **te** | “these / those” | OK | | cose | “things” (plural) | **rzeczy** | “things” | OK | | belle | “beautiful / sweet” (adjective, plural) | **piękne** | “beautiful / sweet” | OK | | sì | resultative “so” (adverb) | **tak** | “so / thus” | OK | | ch’a* (che + a) | causal‑resultative conjunction “that … to” | **aby** | “so that / in order that” | OK | | bene | “good / well” (adverb) | **dobra** | “good” (as adjective modifying *nadzieja*) | OK | | sperar | “to hope” (infinitive) | **nadzieja** | “hope” (noun) | OK | | m'era | clitic + imperf. of *essere*: “to me was” (experiencer) | **dla mnie** | “for me” | OK | | cagione | “occasion / cause” (noun) | **przyczyną** | “cause / occasion” | OK | | di (line 42) | genitive marker “of” linking *quella* and *fiera* | — (case ending on *tej*) | — | UNNECESSARY | | quella | demonstrative “that” (singular) | **tej** | “that” (genitive) | OK | | fiera | “wild beast” (noun, singular) | **bestii** | “beast” (genitive) | OK | | a (line 42) | preposition “with / about” | **o** | “about / concerning” | OK | | la | definite article “the” (feminine singular) | — (no article in Polish) | — | UNNECESSARY | | gaetta | “dappled / speckled” (adjective) | **plamistej** | “dappled / speckled” | OK | | pelle | “skin” (noun, singular) | **skórze** | “skin” (locative) | OK |
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `di` (both occurrences) and `la` – Polish does not use separate prepositions or articles for these genitive/definite functions; the grammatical relation is expressed by noun case endings. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected; all source meanings are represented in the Polish translation, and agreement (gender, number, case) conforms to Polish grammar.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Polish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Polish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
